content: The document titled Guidance on Development and Implementation of a National Deployment and Vaccination Plan for Vaccines Against Pandemic Influenza and Other Respiratory Viruses of Pandemic Potential was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2023. It provides comprehensive recommendations for countries to develop and implement national plans for the deployment and vaccination of pandemic vaccines. This guidance is based on lessons learned from previous pandemics, including the 2009 H1N1 influenza pandemic and the COVID-19 pandemic, and aims to strengthen preparedness and response efforts for future health emergencies. The guidance emphasizes the importance of a National Deployment and Vaccination Plan (NDVP) as a critical tool for ensuring timely, equitable, and efficient vaccine distribution during a pandemic. It highlights the need for countries to adopt a multisectoral approach, aligning NDVPs with broader health emergency preparedness plans, such as respiratory pathogen pandemic preparedness plans and national health security action plans. The document also underscores the value of leveraging global and national expertise to create a coherent and coordinated vaccination strategy. Key objectives of the guidance include facilitating the development of NDVPs, enabling national strategies for accessing pandemic vaccines, compiling lessons learned from past pandemics, and serving as a resource for preparedness and response activities related to emergency vaccination. The guidance outlines a range of technical areas and processes essential for effective vaccine deployment, including legal frameworks, regulatory mechanisms, supply chain management, risk communication, and community engagement. The document also provides a detailed methodology for NDVP development, which is divided into four core phases: inception, development, adoption, and continuous elaboration. These phases involve activities such as establishing multidisciplinary planning committees, conducting situation analyses, and engaging in simulation exercises to test and refine the plan. The guidance encourages countries to integrate NDVPs with other pandemic preparedness plans and to continuously update them based on evolving technologies and lessons learned. The WHO acknowledges the contributions of various stakeholders, including national governments, civil society organizations, international partners, and private sector entities, in the development and implementation of NDVPs. It also highlights the importance of fostering trust with the public and stakeholders to support vaccine acceptance and demand. The guidance document includes a template to assist countries in drafting their NDVPs and a compilation of lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic. It emphasizes the benefits of having a current and relevant NDVP, such as improved preparedness, strengthened health systems, and enhanced coordination during a pandemic response. Overall, the guidance serves as a practical tool for countries to enhance their pandemic preparedness and response capabilities, with a focus on equitable and efficient vaccine deployment. It reflects WHO's commitment to supporting global health security and strengthening health systems to address future pandemics effectively.
